chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Washa', from Muthanna, who said:

We went out to Makkah, so the women caught a dove from the doves of Amaj when we reached Al-Bareed. So the women plucked out its wings. Then they entered Makkah with it. So Abu Baseer went over to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) and informed him, so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Look around for a woman not having a problem with her, so give the bird to her to look after it and keep it. When its wings are straight (grown back), she should free it'.

key_terms.أَمَجَ: a place or type of dove in Makkah
key_terms.الْبَرِيدَ: a station or location near Makkah

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a dove caught in Mecca whose wings are plucked?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the practical application of expiation (kaffarah) for hunting in the Haram, specifically addressing the scenario where a bird's wings are plucked to prevent escape. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes entrusting the bird to a pious woman for care until its wings regenerate, emphasizing the preservation of the animal's life as a form of restitution. This method reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on mercy and the restoration of the hunted creature's natural state before its release.
